title: Literal installation token in a workflow command line
summary: A synthetic ghs_ installation token written as a literal in the text of a workflow step: inside an echo of NAME=value to the GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_OUTPUT environment file, and as the argument of an add-mask workflow command.
rationale: The command names (add-mask, GITHUB_ENV, GITHUB_OUTPUT) and the NAME=value shape read as handling a secret safely, and add-mask is a statement that the value is secret. But the redaction the documentation describes happens on the runner when the job runs; the text of the command line, with the literal in it, is what a repository, a workflow file or a pasted script holds. The contrast is with the same lines carrying a reference or a runner mask (a separate Case), where no token byte is present. The reported range is the token, not the command, the name or the equals sign.

expectation.rationale: Flagged. The value is a credential of the documented token family wherever it is written. The provider documents the environment-file commands as writing NAME=value records and add-mask as redacting a value on the runner; neither statement removes the literal from the command text, so the text still holds the secret.

sources.supports: Setting an environment variable: echo "{environment_variable_name}={value}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"; setting an output parameter: echo "{name}={value}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT".
sources.locator: sections: Setting an environment variable; Setting an output parameter

sources.supports: add-mask takes the value as its argument; when you mask a value, it is treated as a secret and will be redacted on the runner; register it before outputting it in the build logs or using it in any other workflow commands.
sources.locator: section: Masking a value in a log

sources.supports: Format of the ghs_ token family (opaque form of 40 characters; the staged rollout of the ghs_APPID_JWT form).

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. Origin of the inputs: the command shapes are taken from the cited documentation examples (observed); the token is a synthetic value built from an existing authored base; the arrangement of one value in each command shape is evidence-derived, not an observed workflow. No workflow was executed and no value was tested. Whether a consumer reads a workflow file, an environment file or a runner log, and how it treats a mask, is the consumer's measurement contract and is not assumed here. Inference, not a documented statement: that masking at run time does not change the text of a command line stored elsewhere.
